ogch.BaseSchema.tappDefinition.title: Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (TAPP) Definition v3
ogch.BaseSchema.tappDefinition.description: A registered Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (TAPP) definition modeled as a PLAN — prov:Plan / bios:LabProtocol (also cdi:Activity + schema:Action for the DDI-CDI process/action description). It is a reusable procedure that prescribes an analysis; the analysis OCCURRENCE is the prov:Activity in adaProduct.prov:wasGeneratedBy, which references this plan via prov:used. Because the TAPP is a plan, its instrument / bios:computationalTool / bios:reagent are directly-specified resources (not prov:used entities). The TAPP identity (name, technique, instrument, location) lives at the top level. The standard workflow is encoded in schema:actionProcess as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of cdi:Activity + schema:Action steps (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Each workflow step carries its own parameters, reagents, and instruments. TAPP-level parameters that apply across all steps remain at the top level in schema:additionalProperty. Integrates Bioschemas vocabulary for computational tools and reagents, DDI-CDI for activity sequence, and dqv:hasQualityMeasurement for quality metrics.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the namespace prefixes used in a method definition. Required for the document to be a valid JSON-LD instance. Bound prefixes must include schema (always), cdi (DDI-CDI), and ada (ADA vocabulary). Additional prefixes (bios, dqv, prov, skos) are recommended when those vocabularies are used in the body of the definition.

@id.description: Persistent URI for this TAPP definition in the registry.

@type.description: Must include prov:Plan, cdi:Activity, schema:Action, ada:TAPPDefinition, and bios:LabProtocol. The TAPP is a PLAN (prov:Plan / bios:LabProtocol) — a reusable procedure description that prescribes the analysis, NOT the analysis occurrence (that is the prov:Activity in adaProduct.prov:wasGeneratedBy, which references this plan via prov:used). As a plan, its instrument / bios:computationalTool / bios:reagent are directly-specified resources (bios:LabProtocol convention), not prov:used entities.

schema:name.title: Method Name
schema:name.description: Short descriptive name with version (e.g. "JEOL-8530F WDS Major Element Glass v2.1").

schema:identifier.description: DOI or other persistent ID for this method definition.

schema:description.description: Human-readable summary of the method, may be auto-generated from constant parameters at registration time.

schema:datePublished.title: Method Start Date
schema:datePublished.description: ISO 8601 date when this method configuration was first used.

schema:dateModified.description: ISO 8601 date of last update to this definition.

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of the activity type (e.g. schema:CreateAction for a production method).

schema:measurementTechnique.title: Technique
schema:measurementTechnique.description: The analytical technique this method implements. Must be a DefinedTerm from a controlled vocabulary of techniques.

schema:object.description: Target material(s) this method is designed to analyse (e.g. silicate glass, olivine, spinel), modeled as DefinedTerm(s) or free text; and/or the sample(s) analysed, modeled as iSamples material-sample objects (the "Samples analyzed" shape carried over from geochemProduct).

schema:name.description: Sample name/identifier as used in the lab.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Per-sample PropertyValue entries (e.g. analysis location); technique profiles constrain these.

schema:instrument.description: Instrument specification(s) for this method: a single instrument object, or an array of instruments when the method uses more than one (e.g. LA-ICP-MS = a laser ablation system plus the ICP-MS). Use schema:hasPart for instrument sub-components (spectrometers, detectors, ICP source, sample introduction system). Path-driven technique overlays select a specific instrument by schema:additionalType and constrain its sub-component tree.

bios:computationalTool.description: Software tools used for data acquisition, reduction, and processing. Each tool carries name, version, and optional URL.

bios:reagent.description: Reference materials, calibration standards, and chemical reagents used across this method. Reagents specific to a single workflow step should be placed on that step instead.

schema:location.title: Laboratory
schema:location.description: Laboratory where this method was developed. Optional; omit for methods that are instrument-generic.

schema:creator.title: Method Author
schema:creator.description:
Person or organisation who defined or is responsible for this method.
The nested schema:description is OPTIONAL, and where present it records the PROVENANCE OF THIS DEFINITION -- how the TAPP definition itself came to be, as distinct from the method it describes. It is where a definition states that it was transcribed from a published protocol, derived from existing metadata records rather than authored by the laboratory, or produced automatically and reviewed by a person. A laboratory-authored TAPP needs nothing here; a draft assembled from other sources should not be mistaken for one, so it says so. The draft TAPP sidecars target it as the 'Procedure Author Description' row.
It sits on the creator rather than at the root deliberately: the claim is about who produced the definition and how, so it belongs with that agent, and a root-level property would invite a second copy. Note that the {'@id'} branch below is sealed, so a creator given as a bare reference cannot carry it -- a reference names an agent described elsewhere and makes no claim of its own.
The property is DECLARED by the person and organization building blocks this anyOfs, where it is a plain optional string. The note is here rather than there because those two blocks are general-purpose CDIF blocks with five other consumers, and this meaning is specific to a TAPP definition.

schema:actionProcess.description: The standard workflow for this method, expressed as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action describing a distinct phase (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Steps carry their own parameters, reagents, instruments, and sub-steps. Exactly one step must be the sample-preparation step -- see MethodWorkflowHowTo.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Method-level Advanced-protocol parameters that apply across all workflow steps. Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value. Replaces the former ada:methodParameters. Technique TAPP profiles constrain the allowed entries via $refs to the parameterTemplates (specifications) and parameterValues (values) registries. Step-specific parameters should be placed on the appropriate workflow step instead.

ada:targetMaterialTemplate.description:
Template for per-target-material parameters, a target material being a material type this procedure is designed to analyse (Silicate mineral, Silicate glass, Oxide, Sulfide, Carbonate, Phosphate, Metal or alloy). Declares the target-material domain and the columns that repeat over it.
The domain is declared by the TAPP's Target Material field, marked `defines: target material`; the fields keyed BY it are the electron-beam conditions (Beam Current, Beam Mode, Beam Diameter, Beam Raster Dimensions, Beam Damage Minimization), and Primary Calibration Standard Name is keyed `target material x target species`.
Target materials are assumed present in any sample the procedure would analyse. The binding between a particular sampling unit and the material it hit is instance data, not procedure metadata, so it is recorded as a data-table column and NOT here -- this template carries only the kinds of material expected and the values that repeat over them.

ada:targetMaterialColumns.description: Columns of the per-target-material parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "targetMaterial" that identifies the material named in each row.

ada:targetMaterialDeclaration.description: The material types analysed, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose, and the counterpart of ada:targetSpeciesDeclaration: a submitter may name the materials as a list, or as prose that names none individually. ada:defaultTargetMaterials carries the members that could be recognised; this carries the statement they were recognised FROM, so a cell that parses only in part loses nothing.

ada:defaultTargetMaterials.description:
The material types this procedure targets by default - the ROWS of the per-material table, and the domain `defines: target material` enumerates. An entry is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm naming the material, or a row object binding that material to per-material values.
A row object is keyed throughout by the schema:valueName of the columns declared in ada:targetMaterialColumns, and MUST carry the 'targetMaterial' key - the column that sibling description requires to identify the material named in each row.
Column-level constraints stay on the column: schema:readonlyValue when a value is constant across every material, and schema:defaultValue when one default serves the whole column. Use a row only for values that differ between materials.

anyOf.title: Per-target-material row
anyOf.description: One row of the per-material table, keyed by column schema:valueName. null records a value that is deliberately absent for this material rather than merely unstated.

targetMaterial.description: The material type this row is for (e.g. "Silicate mineral"), from the controlled list the TAPP's Target Material field offers, optionally qualified in the same cell. The key is the schema:valueName of the identifier column, which ada:targetMaterialColumns requires exactly one of, so a row is keyed by column valueName throughout.

ada:targetSpeciesTemplate.description: Template for per-target-species (element-specific) parameters. Defines the columns that appear in the species table, each with scope, datatype, and constraints. Target-species rows become schema:variableMeasured entries in metadata records. Typically associated with the acquisition workflow step.

ada:targetSpeciesColumns.description: Columns of the per-target-species parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "targetSpecies" that identifies the analyzed constituent named in each row.

ada:targetSpeciesDeclaration.description: What this procedure analyses, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose, and the counterpart of ada:collectorConfiguration on the instrument side: submitters write the target species as a list, as a list with a sentence attached ("Mn (55Mn), Fe (57Fe) ... Pb (207Pb) in seawater"), or as prose that names no species individually at all ("Major and trace elements, masses 23-75"). ada:defaultTargetSpecies below carries the members that could be recognised; this carries the statement they were recognised FROM, so a cell that parses only in part loses nothing. Present whenever the declaration said more than the parsed rows record.

ada:defaultTargetSpecies.description:
The target species (analyzed constituents) this method targets by default — the ROWS of the per-species table. An entry is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm naming the species, or a row object binding that species to per-species values.
A row object is keyed throughout by the schema:valueName of the columns declared in ada:targetSpeciesColumns, and MUST carry the 'targetSpecies' key - the column that sibling description requires to identify the constituent named in each row.
Which values belong here follows the TAPP's Analysis-Level Tier. A column marked Read-Only is fixed by the procedure, so its value belongs on the row. A column marked Editable takes a starting value here that an analysis may override; the value actually used is reported per result, as a column of the data table, and surfaces as schema:variableMeasured on the data product. Values that vary per result and are not defaulted do not belong here at all.
Column-level constraints stay on the column: schema:readonlyValue when a value is constant across every target species, and schema:defaultValue when one default serves the whole column. Use a row only for values that differ between target species.

anyOf.title: Per-species row
anyOf.description: One row of the per-species table, keyed by column schema:valueName. null records a value that is deliberately absent for this species rather than merely unstated.

targetSpecies.description:
The analyzed constituent this row is for (e.g. "SiO2"). The key is the schema:valueName of the identifier column, which ada:targetSpeciesColumns requires exactly one of, so a row is keyed by column valueName throughout.
This key was 'analyte' until 2026-09-25. The rename moved the COLUMN's schema:valueName const to 'targetSpecies' but left the row half behind, so a row object could satisfy neither half: keyed 'analyte' it contradicted its own column, keyed 'targetSpecies' it failed this required. Nothing upstream caught it because every tappDefinition example lists bare strings here and so never exercises this branch; it surfaced against the 46 stored ADA method definitions, which do use row objects.

ada:monitoredPropertyTemplate.description: Template for per-monitored-property parameters, a monitored property being an instrument selection position (a mass, a Faraday cup, an energy-loss edge, an X-ray line). Declares the monitored-property domain and the columns that repeat over it. The domain is declared by different fields per technique -- Monitored Isotopes for ICP-MS, Collector Configuration for MC-ICP-MS, EELS Edges for TEM.

ada:monitoredPropertyColumns.description:
Columns of the per-monitored-property table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "monitoredProperty" identifying the selection position named in each row. ("channel" was that name before the 2026-09 rename.)
A 'collector' column is the optional one worth knowing about: it maps each monitored property to the collector that carries it. That mapping is procedure CONFIGURATION, not instrument hardware -- the same array can be wired differently by another procedure, and an analysis may override it -- which is why it belongs here on the method definition and not on schema:instrument. The collectors themselves are hardware and live there, in hasPart[Collector].ada:collectors; this column's values are their schema:name.

anyOf.title: Per-monitored-property row
anyOf.description: One row of the table, keyed by column schema:valueName.

monitoredProperty.description: The selection position measured, e.g. '⁸⁴Sr'. Becomes a schema:variableMeasured entry on the data product.

targetSpecies.description: The species this property helps determine, when it determines one. Absent for a monitor.

collector.description: schema:name of the collector carrying this property, matching an entry in schema:instrument…hasPart[Collector].ada:collectors.

ada:reportedPropertyTemplate.description: Template for the variables this procedure REPORTS and their units, as distinct from ada:targetSpeciesTemplate which records what was acquired. Declares the reported-property domain and the columns that repeat over it. It also states the procedure's scope boundary: a derived quantity inside this list is in scope, anything beyond it belongs to a separate, coupled procedure.

ada:reportedPropertyColumns.description: Columns of the reported-property table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "reportedProperty" identifying the reported variable named in each row.

ada:defaultReportedProperties.description: The reported properties this procedure defines by default — the ROWS of the reported- property table. Each is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm identifying the property; per-property column VALUES live in the analysis record, not here.

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements that characterize the method's expected performance (e.g. analytical precision, accuracy, counting statistics error). Uses the CDIF qualityMeasure building block.

schema:relatedLink.title: Method References
schema:relatedLink.description: Publications, Zenodo records, or other references reports describing or evaluating this method.

schema:variableMeasured.title: Reported Variables
schema:variableMeasured.description: Variables / properties this procedure reports (e.g. detection limit, limit of quantification, calibration factor, uncertainty propagation method), each modeled as a schema:PropertyValueSpecification (a procedure-level default, carrying schema:defaultValue) or a schema:PropertyValue (a measured value, carrying schema:value), keyed by schema:name. A technique profile enumerates the reported properties it defines; a dataset instance overrides each schema:defaultValue with a schema:value. Left open here — the technique overlay narrows it.

WorkflowHowTo.description: The method's standard workflow expressed as a schema:HowTo. Contains an ordered array of workflow steps in schema:step, where each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action.

schema:name.description: Name of the workflow (e.g. "EPMA WDS analytical workflow").

schema:url.description: URL to a published protocol document.

schema:step.description: Ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action + schema:HowToStep describing a distinct phase of the analytical procedure. This shape carries NO sample-preparation requirement, because it is used for a STEP's sub-workflow as well as for a method's top-level workflow; see MethodWorkflowHowTo for the method form that does require one.

MethodWorkflowHowTo.description:
A method's standard workflow: a WorkflowHowTo that must also include exactly one sample-preparation step (schema:name "Sample preparation" with schema:additionalType containing "bios:LabProcess"); its schema:position is left to the protocol author.
Separate from WorkflowHowTo because that shape is ALSO the sub-workflow of a single step (WorkflowStep.schema:actionProcess), and requiring sample preparation there is wrong -- a step's sub-workflow is the breakdown of that one step, so a sample-preparation step broken into mount / grind / polish / coat would have needed a nested "Sample preparation" inside itself. Both references pointed at one $def, so the method's requirement reached every sub-workflow. Nothing exercised it, as no example nests a sub-workflow.

contains.description: a sample preparation step is required.

WorkflowStep.description: A single step in the analytical workflow, modeled as a cdi:Activity + schema:Action. Each step describes a distinct phase such as sample preparation, instrument calibration, data acquisition, data processing, or quality control. Steps carry their own parameters, instruments, reagents, and may contain sub-steps via schema:actionProcess.

@type.description: All THREE are required. cdi:Activity and schema:Action carry the DDI-CDI and schema.org process semantics this model is built on; schema:HowToStep is what schema.org itself expects of a value of schema:step on a schema:HowTo, and omitting it made these steps invalid against the plain schema.org reading -- and against the base cdifProvActivity, whose own step shape requires schema:HowToStep. The two shapes disagreed, which is observable in the examples: 565 steps carried cdi:Activity + schema:Action and 15 carried schema:HowToStep, depending on which side emitted them.

schema:name.description: Name of this workflow step (e.g. "Sample preparation").

schema:description.description: Detailed description of what this step involves.

schema:position.description: Ordinal position in the workflow sequence (1-based).

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for wet-lab steps, schema:CreateAction for production steps). A CURIE may also be written as a JSON-LD IRI reference, which is what CDIF's schemaorgProperties/additionalProperty SHACL asks for; the `contains` on the method's schema:step accepts either serialization, so widening here cannot orphan the sample-preparation requirement.

schema:instrument.description: Instrument or equipment used in this step.

bios:computationalTool.description: Software tools used in this step.

bios:reagent.description: Reference materials, standards, or reagents used in this step.

prov:used.description: Input entities consumed or referenced by this step (e.g. prepared sample from a prior step).

schema:result.description: Output entity produced by this step (can be referenced as input by a subsequent step).

schema:object.description: Reference to a prior step whose result is the input for this step (action chaining).

schema:additionalProperty.description: Step-specific parameters (e.g. beam conditions for the acquisition step, matrix correction settings for the data processing step). Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value.

schema:actionProcess.description: Sub-workflow for this step, expressed as a nested schema:HowTo with its own ordered steps. Use for steps that have a multi-phase internal procedure (e.g. sample preparation with mount, grind, polish, coat).

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements specific to this workflow step.

MethodParameter.description: A parameter specification for the method, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. Uses schema.org properties for value constraints (defaultValue, minValue, maxValue, readonlyValue, valueRequired) and ada: extensions for analytical method semantics (fieldScope, category, tier). Link to a controlled vocabulary via schema:inDefinedTermSet.

schema:description.description: Guidance text shown to the user in the form.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. Links to a skos:Concept or similar term definition. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant, fixed for every session (read-only in form). false = editable (default or optional depending on valueRequired).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided (mandatory). false = optional. Combined with readonlyValue: readonly+required = constant mandatory; !readonly+required = editable mandatory; !readonly+!required = optional.

schema:minValue.description: Minimum allowed numeric value. Defines the lower bound of a valid range at the method level; specific values within this range may be set per element in ada:targetSpeciesTemplate.

schema:maxValue.description: Maximum allowed numeric value. Upper bound of valid range.

schema:stepValue.description: Granularity expected of the value (e.g. 0.1 for nA).

schema:valuePattern.description: Regex pattern for validating string values.

schema:multipleValues.description: Whether multiple values are allowed (default false).

ada:fieldScope.description: Whether this parameter is fixed at the method level, varies per analytical session, or is element-specific.

ada:category.description: Grouping label for form layout (e.g. "Beam Conditions", "Data Processing", "Quality Control"). String for simple cases; DefinedTerm to link to a controlled vocabulary of parameter categories.

ada:dataType.description: Expected data type for the parameter value.

schema:unitCode.description: URI for unit of measure (QUDT preferred).

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: The CDIF building block property path this parameter maps to. Used for JSON-LD serialisation.

ada:tier.description: Mandatory / Recommended / Optional tier from the metadata profile. Informs validation strictness.

MethodParameterValue.description: A read-only method parameter carrying the fixed protocol value, typed as schema:PropertyValue. Used for Advanced-protocol parameters that the analyst cannot change (the value is set by the protocol). The value is in schema:value; the human-readable label is in schema:name. Contrast with MethodParameter (schema:PropertyValueSpecification), used for editable parameters.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:value.description: The fixed protocol value for this read-only parameter.

KeyedTableColumn.description: Definition of one column of a KEYED TABLE, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. A keyed table has one row per member of some domain -- a target species, a reported property, a monitored property -- and one column per field whose value repeats over that domain (the TAPP workbook's `Keyed By` column). Rows become schema:variableMeasured entries; columns become schema:additionalProperty within each. TargetSpeciesColumn and ReportedPropertyColumn are the two domains modelled so far; both are this shape.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this column's parameter type in a formal vocabulary. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this column. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: Default value for this column (pre-filled per row).

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant across all target species (read-only column).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided for every target-species row.

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: How this column maps into the variableMeasured JSON-LD structure.

TargetSpeciesColumn.description: One column of the per-target-species parameter table. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn; kept as its own name because generated schemas and the shared targetSpeciesColumns registry $ref it.

TargetMaterialColumn.description: One column of the per-target-material parameter table. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn; kept as its own name because generated schemas and the shared targetMaterialColumns registry $ref it.

ReportedPropertyColumn.description: One column of the reported-property table. The reported properties are what the procedure REPORTS -- '206Pb/238U date (Ma)', 'd56Fe (permil vs IRMM-014)' -- as distinct from the target species and monitored properties it ACQUIRES. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn.

MonitoredPropertyColumn.description: One column of the monitored-property table. A monitored property is an instrument SELECTION POSITION -- a mass, a Faraday cup, an energy-loss edge, an X-ray line. It is not a flavour of target species: the target species is what is measured, the monitored property is the position it is measured on, and the two are independent. One target species may occupy several monitored properties, and MC-ICP-MS cups routinely monitor interferences that are not target species at all. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn.

MonitoredPropertyIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory monitored-property-identifier column, naming the selection position in each row. Mirrors TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn and ReportedPropertyIdentifierColumn; like both it maps into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name, because the variable list is shared across a procedure's table parts rather than owned by any one of them.

ReportedPropertyIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory reported-property identifier column, naming the reported variable in each row. Mirrors TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn: pinned constants fix the column's role as a row identifier rather than an editable parameter. Both identifier columns map into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name because the variable list is SHARED -- a procedure yields several tables (target species, monitored property, reported property) over one logical variable registry, not one table per document.

TargetMaterialIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory target-material-identifier column, naming the material type in each row. Mirrors TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn and MonitoredPropertyIdentifierColumn; like both it maps into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name, because the material a sampling unit hit is recorded as a column of the data table -- the variable list is shared across a procedure's table parts rather than owned by any one of them.

TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory target-species-identifier column. Each row in the species table must carry a value for this column naming the analyzed constituent (e.g. "SiO2", "Fe"). Pinned constants enforce the column's role: readonly (the identifier of a row, not an editable parameter), required, mandatory tier, and a fixed mapping into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name. Long-term the value space should be a DefinedTermSet; for now a string.

ComputationalTool.description: Software application used for data acquisition, reduction, or processing. Follows Bioschemas ComputationalTool pattern.

schema:name.description: Name of the software (e.g. "Probe for EPMA").

schema:description.description: Role or purpose of this tool in the method.

schema:url.description: URL to the software product or documentation.

ada:toolRole.description: Role this software plays in the analytical workflow.

Reagent.description: A reference material, calibration standard, or chemical reagent. Follows Bioschemas reagent pattern with extensions for geochemistry reference materials.

@type.description: What the material IS, independent of the role it plays here (that is ada:reagentRole). One of the three kinds must be present: schema:DefinedTerm for a material identified by a registry entry (GeoReM, NIST SRM, USGS); schema:Product for a specific catalogued specimen or purchased lot (Smithsonian NMNH number, IGSN, in-house standard); schema:ChemicalSubstance for a bulk chemical or coating stock.

schema:name.description: Name of the material (e.g. "San Carlos olivine").

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).

schema:termCode.description: Registry code for the material on the schema:DefinedTerm path (e.g. "SRM 610", "ATHO-G").

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The registry the schema:termCode belongs to (GeoReM, NIST SRM catalogue, USGS RM list).

ada:reagentRole.description: Role of this material in the method.

schema:citation.description: Publication reference for the standard's accepted values.

PropertyIDValue.description:
One value of schema:propertyID: a vocabulary URI, a JSON-LD IRI reference, or a DefinedTerm.
Whether the property holding these is an ARRAY depends on which job schema:PropertyValue is doing, because schema.org overloads that one class for several things that ought to be distinct (see the CDIF Core Implementation Guide, "Polymorphism of PropertyValue"):

  * schema:additionalProperty and schema:variableMeasured -- a measured or declared parameter.
    propertyID is 0..* there, so it is ALWAYS an array and a consumer iterates without first
    testing the value's type.
  * schema:identifier -- an identifier for the identifier scheme (DOI, ARK, IGSN). Upstream
    types that one as a bare string or {"@id": ...}, never an array, so do NOT wrap it.

ogch.registry.parameterTemplates.title: ADA Method-Parameter Template Registry
ogch.registry.parameterTemplates.description: Registry of reusable schema:PropertyValueSpecification method-parameter templates derived from technique TAPP spreadsheets. Each $def constrains one method-level (readOnly:true) parameter template (e.g. DriftCorrection, massAbsorptionCoefficients). TAPP building blocks reference these definitions via fragment $refs (schema.yaml#/$defs/<name>) so they resolve locally through the building-block register. The root only hosts $defs; it has no instantiable properties of its own.

aiva_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDefau.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
aiva_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDefau.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

epma_backgroundPositionDefault.title: Background Position(s)

epma_countingStatisticsErrorDefault.title: Counting Statistics Error

epma_driftCorrectionDefault.title: Drift Correction

epma_halogenCorrectionOnOxygenDefault.title: Halogen Correction on Oxygen
epma_halogenCorrectionOnOxygenDefault.description: Whether oxygen content was adjusted to account for halogen substitution (F and/or Cl replacing OH) in halogen-bearing phases such as apatite, amphibole, and mica, where oxygen is calculated by stoichiometry.

epma_normalizationStandardsBasedCorrecti.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction

laMcicpmsUPb_ageDatumReferenceEpochDefau.title: Age Datum / Reference Epoch

enum: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

laMcicpmsUPb_collisionReactionGasMixture.description: Where the collision or reaction cell is supplied with a mixture of gases rather than a single gas, the identities and proportions of that mixture. Recorded separately from the gas identity. Record 'N/A' where a single gas is used.

laMcicpmsUPb_countingStatisticsErrorDefa.title: Counting Statistics Error

laMcicpmsUPb_doubleSpikeMixingRatioDefau.title: Double-Spike Mixing Ratio
laMcicpmsUPb_doubleSpikeMixingRatioDefau.description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total target species signal in the spiked mixture, expressed as spike fraction (0–1) or spike:sample ratio. The optimum is target species-system specific and is typically determined using the Double Spike Toolbox or equivalent. The achieved mixing ratio may deviate from the target within acceptable bounds (typically ±20% of optimal); the double-spike inversion corrects for actual mixing ratios. Record 'N/A' where the procedure does not use a double spike.

laMcicpmsUPb_doublyChargedSpeciesMonitor.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
laMcicpmsUPb_doublyChargedSpeciesMonitor.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning. The monitor species and the mass positions monitored should be stated explicitly. Analogous to Oxide Production Method and Threshold for oxide monitoring.

laMcicpmsUPb_doublyChargedSpeciesProduct.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
laMcicpmsUPb_doublyChargedSpeciesProduct.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning. The acceptable threshold is typically <1% or <3%. Record both the threshold and the measured value.

laMcicpmsUPb_errorCorrelationBetweenRepo.title: Error Correlation Between Reported Quantities
laMcicpmsUPb_errorCorrelationBetweenRepo.description: The correlation coefficient between pairs of reported quantities whose uncertainties are not independent, together with the pair it applies to and how it was obtained.

laMcicpmsUPb_fusionFluxAndDilutionRatioD.title: Fusion Flux and Dilution Ratio
laMcicpmsUPb_fusionFluxAndDilutionRatioD.description: For procedures using fused glass, the flux type and sample:flux dilution ratio used to prepare the analytical glass.

laMcicpmsUPb_icpTuningDefault.title: ICP Tuning
laMcicpmsUPb_icpTuningDefault.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).

laMcicpmsUPb_instrumentSerialNumberOrLab.title: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier
laMcicpmsUPb_instrumentSerialNumberOrLab.description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit.

enum: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier

laMcicpmsUPb_internalAnalyticalPrecision.title: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
laMcicpmsUPb_internalAnalyticalPrecision.description: Precision of a single measurement, derived from the scatter of the cycles, sweeps or integrations that make it up, together with the method used to assess it. State the statistic (2SE, 2SD, 1s RSD), the number of cycles it is computed over, and the reported quantity it applies to. Distinct from Counting Statistics Error, which records the uncertainty predicted from the counts rather than the scatter observed; where a procedure reports both, record the observed value here and the predicted value there.

enum: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

laMcicpmsUPb_laserEnergyDefault.title: Laser Energy
laMcicpmsUPb_laserEnergyDefault.description: Laser pulse energy in millijoules as set at the laser output or measured at the sample surface. Report only when the system displays energy directly. Laser fluence (J cm⁻²) is the preferred quantity and is captured in Laser Fluence (Energy Density).

laMcicpmsUPb_limitOfQuantificationMethod.title: Limit of Quantification (LOQ) Method
laMcicpmsUPb_limitOfQuantificationMethod.description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification (LOQ): the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy. Required when concentrations near the LOD are reported.

laMcicpmsUPb_makeUpGasAndFlowRateDefault.title: Make-up Gas and Flow Rate
laMcicpmsUPb_makeUpGasAndFlowRateDefault.description: Supplementary gas added to the sample-carrying stream between the sample introduction system and the plasma, with its identity and the procedure-registered target flow rate. Record any small nitrogen or hydrogen addition with its own flow, whose unit commonly differs from the make-up flow. Record 'None' explicitly where no supplementary gas is added, to distinguish it from not reported.

laMcicpmsUPb_memoryEffectMitigationDefau.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
laMcicpmsUPb_memoryEffectMitigationDefau.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.

laMcicpmsUPb_normalizationStandardsBased.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction
laMcicpmsUPb_normalizationStandardsBased.description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.

laMcicpmsUPb_numberOfReplicatesDefault.title: Number of Replicates
laMcicpmsUPb_numberOfReplicatesDefault.description: Number of replicate measurements performed on the same sample, or on the same nominal location where the technique is spatially resolved. For spot analysis this is the number of individual spots per grain or location; for transects, the number of replicate lines; for mapping, the number of map acquisitions of the same area; for solution work, the number of discrete replicate measurements acquired per sample solution.

laMcicpmsUPb_preAblationSurfaceTreatment.title: Pre-Ablation Surface Treatment
laMcicpmsUPb_preAblationSurfaceTreatment.description: Procedure applied immediately before each analysis to remove surface contamination or condition the sample surface. Distinct from general sample preparation. For spot analysis, pre-ablation pulses are discarded before signal acquisition begins. For mapping, this step is typically omitted.

laMcicpmsUPb_preAnalysisImagingAndScreen.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
laMcicpmsUPb_preAnalysisImagingAndScreen.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

laMcicpmsUPb_reactionGasFlowRateDefault.title: Reaction Gas Flow Rate
laMcicpmsUPb_reactionGasFlowRateDefault.description: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC), in mL/min. Record 'None' if DRC mode is not used, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include DRC or the instrument has no cell.

laMcicpmsUPb_signalSmoothingDefault.title: Signal Smoothing
laMcicpmsUPb_signalSmoothingDefault.description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability. For mapping analyses, report "None" explicitly.

laMcicpmsUPb_spikeOutlierFilteringApproa.title: Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach
laMcicpmsUPb_spikeOutlierFilteringApproa.description: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous data - signal spikes, individual cycles, or whole replicate measurements - before the reported value is calculated. State where in the reduction sequence the filter is applied.

laMcicpmsUPb_torchDepthDefault.title: Torch Depth
laMcicpmsUPb_torchDepthDefault.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer.

laMcicpmsUPb_transectRateMappingRateOrSt.title: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size
laMcicpmsUPb_transectRateMappingRateOrSt.description: For continuous line scan (transect) and raster mapping: the stage translation speed in µm s⁻¹. For mapping, the mapping rate (mm² h⁻¹) may be reported as an alternative when scan speed is session-variable. For stepped line profiles: the distance between successive spot positions in µm.

enum: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size

laMcicpmsUPb_uncertaintyPropagationMetho.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
laMcicpmsUPb_uncertaintyPropagationMetho.description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.

enum: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size

laSficpmsUPb_uncertaintyPropagationMetho.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
laSficpmsUPb_uncertaintyPropagationMetho.description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.

laSficpms_betweenSessionAnalyticalPrecis.title: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
laSficpms_betweenSessionAnalyticalPrecis.description: Precision of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months — long-term or intermediate precision — and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values, specifying the reference material, the number of measurements and sessions, the time span covered, and the statistic reported.

enum: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

laSficpms_countingStatisticsErrorDefault.title: Counting Statistics Error
laSficpms_countingStatisticsErrorDefault.description: Uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — for each reported quantity per analysis, with the sigma level stated. Derived from the counts on the target species together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. Distinct from the scatter actually observed within a measurement or between repeated measurements, which is recorded separately.

laSficpms_detectionLimitDefault.title: Detection Limit
laSficpms_detectionLimitDefault.description: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per target species, these being the same set). State the units and whether the values are procedure-typical estimates or session-specific measured values. The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations.

laSficpms_doublyChargedSpeciesMonitorDef.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
laSficpms_doublyChargedSpeciesMonitorDef.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning. The monitor species and the mass positions monitored should be stated explicitly. Analogous to Oxide Production Method and Threshold for oxide monitoring.

laSficpms_doublyChargedSpeciesProduction.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
laSficpms_doublyChargedSpeciesProduction.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning. The acceptable threshold is typically <1% or <3%. Record both the threshold and the measured value.

laSficpms_fusionFluxAndDilutionRatioDefa.title: Fusion Flux and Dilution Ratio
laSficpms_fusionFluxAndDilutionRatioDefa.description: For procedures using fused glass, the flux type and sample:flux dilution ratio used to prepare the analytical glass.

laSficpms_icpTuningDefault.title: ICP Tuning
laSficpms_icpTuningDefault.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).

laSficpms_instrumentSerialNumberOrLabIde.title: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier
laSficpms_instrumentSerialNumberOrLabIde.description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit.

enum: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier

laSficpms_internalAnalyticalPrecisionAnd.title: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
laSficpms_internalAnalyticalPrecisionAnd.description: Precision of a single measurement, derived from the scatter of the cycles, sweeps or integrations that make it up, together with the method used to assess it. State the statistic (2SE, 2SD, 1s RSD), the number of cycles it is computed over, and the reported quantity it applies to. Distinct from Counting Statistics Error, which records the uncertainty predicted from the counts rather than the scatter observed; where a procedure reports both, record the observed value here and the predicted value there.

enum: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

laSficpms_laserEnergyDefault.title: Laser Energy
laSficpms_laserEnergyDefault.description: Laser pulse energy in millijoules as set at the laser output or measured at the sample surface. Report only when the system displays energy directly. Laser fluence (J cm⁻²) is the preferred quantity and is captured in Laser Fluence (Energy Density).

laSficpms_limitOfQuantificationMethodDef.title: Limit of Quantification (LOQ) Method
laSficpms_limitOfQuantificationMethodDef.description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification (LOQ): the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy. Required when concentrations near the LOD are reported.

laSficpms_makeUpGasAndFlowRateDefault.title: Make-up Gas and Flow Rate
laSficpms_makeUpGasAndFlowRateDefault.description: Supplementary gas added to the sample-carrying stream between the sample introduction system and the plasma, with its identity and the procedure-registered target flow rate. Record any small nitrogen or hydrogen addition with its own flow, whose unit commonly differs from the make-up flow. Record 'None' explicitly where no supplementary gas is added, to distinguish it from not reported.

laSficpms_memoryEffectMitigationDefault.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
laSficpms_memoryEffectMitigationDefault.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.

laSficpms_normalizationStandardsBasedCor.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction
laSficpms_normalizationStandardsBasedCor.description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.

laSficpms_numberOfReplicatesDefault.title: Number of Replicates
laSficpms_numberOfReplicatesDefault.description: Number of replicate measurements performed on the same sample, or on the same nominal location where the technique is spatially resolved. For spot analysis this is the number of individual spots per grain or location; for transects, the number of replicate lines; for mapping, the number of map acquisitions of the same area; for solution work, the number of discrete replicate measurements acquired per sample solution.

laSficpms_preAblationSurfaceTreatmentDef.title: Pre-Ablation Surface Treatment
laSficpms_preAblationSurfaceTreatmentDef.description: Procedure applied immediately before each analysis to remove surface contamination or condition the sample surface. Distinct from general sample preparation. For spot analysis, pre-ablation pulses are discarded before signal acquisition begins. For mapping, this step is typically omitted.

laSficpms_preAnalysisImagingAndScreening.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
laSficpms_preAnalysisImagingAndScreening.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

laSficpms_pulseAnalogDetectorNonlinearit.title: Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Correction
laSficpms_pulseAnalogDetectorNonlinearit.description: Whether a correction was applied for nonlinear detector response at the transition between pulse-counting and analog (and Faraday, for triple-mode instruments) detection modes. Cross-calibration factors between detector modes must be confirmed, typically measured each session. Record 'Applied' and describe the method, the detector modes involved and the target species affected; 'None' where a crossover exists on this instrument but no correction was made, giving the reason; and 'N/A' where the detector is pulse-counting only and no crossover exists.

laSficpms_signalSmoothingDefault.title: Signal Smoothing
laSficpms_signalSmoothingDefault.description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability. For mapping analyses, report "None" explicitly.

laSficpms_spikeOutlierFilteringApproachD.title: Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach
laSficpms_spikeOutlierFilteringApproachD.description: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous data - signal spikes, individual cycles, or whole replicate measurements - before the reported value is calculated. State where in the reduction sequence the filter is applied.

laSficpms_torchDepthDefault.title: Torch Depth
laSficpms_torchDepthDefault.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer.

laSficpms_transectRateMappingRateOrStepS.title: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size
laSficpms_transectRateMappingRateOrStepS.description: For continuous line scan (transect) and raster mapping: the stage translation speed in µm s⁻¹. For mapping, the mapping rate (mm² h⁻¹) may be reported as an alternative when scan speed is session-variable. For stepped line profiles: the distance between successive spot positions in µm.

enum: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size

laSficpms_uncertaintyPropagationMethodDe.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
laSficpms_uncertaintyPropagationMethodDe.description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.

labxct_beamHardeningCorrectionParameterD.title: Beam Hardening Correction Parameter
labxct_beamHardeningCorrectionParameterD.description: Numerical value or setting applied in the software beam hardening correction algorithm for this specific analysis. Companion to Beam Hardening Correction Method.

labxct_crossValidationProcedureRequireme.title: Cross-Validation Procedure Requirement
labxct_crossValidationProcedureRequireme.description: Specification of what independent analytical validation is required to confirm CT segmentation results, phase identification, or quantitative measurements. Common approaches include BSE imaging, SEM-EDS or EPMA modal analysis, He pycnometry for bulk porosity, and Raman or SIMS phase mapping. Record the required validation method(s) and the sampling fraction (e.g., every sample, one per session, or a representative subset).

labxct_ctNumberCalibrationDefault.title: CT Number Calibration
labxct_ctNumberCalibrationDefault.description: Whether the raw CT grayscale values have been calibrated to physically meaningful units using reference materials.

labxct_detectorBinningDefault.title: Detector Binning
labxct_detectorBinningDefault.description: Detector pixel binning factor applied during acquisition. Binning combines adjacent pixels (e.g., 2×2 combines 4 pixels into one).

labxct_framesAveragedPerProjectionDefaul.title: Frames Averaged per Projection
labxct_framesAveragedPerProjectionDefaul.description: Number of individual detector frames acquired and averaged to produce each saved projection image. The effective exposure per projection = exposure time per frame × frames averaged.

labxct_outputBitDepthDefault.title: Output Bit Depth
labxct_outputBitDepthDefault.description: Bit depth of the reconstructed 3D volume (number of bits used to encode each voxel's grayscale value). Common values are 8-bit (256 gray levels), 16-bit (65,536 gray levels), or 32-bit floating point. A required output bit depth may be specified if downstream analysis workflows depend on a consistent grayscale range.

labxct_partialVolumeEffectCriteriaDefaul.title: Partial Volume Effect Criteria
labxct_partialVolumeEffectCriteriaDefaul.description: Specification of how partial volume effects (PVE) are managed in quantitative analysis. PVE correction can be implemented via PSF-based deconvolution tools such as Blob3D. Record the minimum feature size criterion adopted for the procedure (in voxels or µm), the basis for it, the treatment of boundary voxels in modal abundance or size distribution calculations, and whether PVE correction is required or optional. State whether the criterion follows the Withers et al. (2021) convention — a feature must span at least 3 voxels to be positively identified and at least 10 for reliable shape and volume characterisation — or is SNR-limited, PVE-limited or analyst-defined.

labxct_phaseIdentificationMethodDefault.title: Phase Identification Method
labxct_phaseIdentificationMethodDefault.description: Method used to assign reconstructed CT number ranges to specific mineral phases or material types. Approaches include comparison to calculated linear attenuation coefficients (LAC), cross-validation with independent analytical techniques, or empirical calibration.

labxct_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDef.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
labxct_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDef.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

labxct_reconstructionConvolutionFilterDe.title: Reconstruction Convolution Filter
labxct_reconstructionConvolutionFilterDe.description: Convolution (apodization) filter kernel applied during back-projection reconstruction.

labxct_ringArtifactCorrectionMethodDefau.title: Ring Artifact Correction Method
labxct_ringArtifactCorrectionMethodDefau.description: Procedure specification for how ring artifacts are handled. Whether correction was applied and its outcome are recorded separately in Group 6.

labxct_rotationStepSizeDefault.title: Rotation Step Size
labxct_rotationStepSizeDefault.description: Angular increment between successive projection images, in degrees. Equal to Rotation Range divided by Number of Projections when both are reported; however, some sources report step size as the primary rotation parameter without stating the total number of projections explicitly.

labxct_sampleDimensionsDefault.title: Sample Dimensions (L × W × H)
labxct_sampleDimensionsDefault.description: Physical dimensions of the sample in mm, reported as length × width × height (or equivalent three orthogonal measurements).

labxct_sampleMountingMethodDefault.title: Sample Mounting Method
labxct_sampleMountingMethodDefault.description: Method used to mount or hold the sample on the instrument rotation stage. Mounting material should transmit X-rays at the selected voltage without dominating beam attenuation. Report the holder CLASS from the list and name the specific vessel or material alongside it — 'Tube or vial — 1 cm plastic straw', not 'Tube or vial'. Where the sample is sealed or bagged inside a further holder for contamination control, record both layers. Report any adhesive, support material and alignment aids used.

labxct_segmentationThresholdValuesOrCrit.title: Segmentation Threshold Values or Criteria
labxct_segmentationThresholdValuesOrCrit.description: Specific CT number range(s) or quantitative criteria used to define each segmented phase or feature. For LAC-calibrated datasets, report values in cm⁻¹.

labxct_sourceToDetectorDistanceDefault.title: Source-to-Detector Distance (SDD)
labxct_sourceToDetectorDistanceDefault.description: Distance from the X-ray source focal spot to the detector surface, in mm. Voxel size ≈ detector pixel size / M (before binning; divide additionally by optical objective for Versa-class systems).

labxct_sourceToObjectDistanceDefault.title: Source-to-Object Distance (SOD)
labxct_sourceToObjectDistanceDefault.description: Distance from the X-ray source focal spot to the centre of the sample rotation axis, in mm.

labxct_voiSelectionCriteriaDefault.title: VOI Selection Criteria
labxct_voiSelectionCriteriaDefault.description: Rules specifying how the Volume of Interest (VOI) is to be defined for quantitative analysis. Common criteria exclude cone-beam artifact zones at sample edges, beam hardening halos near dense inclusions, and sample holder signal. The actual VOI applied in a specific analysis is recorded separately at analysis level.

labxct_xRayPowerDefault.title: X-ray Power
labxct_xRayPowerDefault.description: X-ray tube power in watts (W). Derivable as voltage (kV) × current (mA) = kV × µA / 1000. If power was varied across samples within the session, report the full range applied (e.g., 7–13 W).

semComposition_analyticalAccuracyDefault.title: Analytical Accuracy
semComposition_analyticalAccuracyDefault.description: Offset between measured and accepted reference values for secondary standards, expressed as percent relative bias. Include reference material, reference value source, and the measured value.

semComposition_analyticalPrecisionDefaul.title: Analytical Precision
semComposition_analyticalPrecisionDefaul.description: Reproducibility of repeated measurements on the same or equivalent reference material, expressed as 1-sigma relative standard deviation (%). Include reference material name, number of analyses (n), and the measured value.

semComposition_backgroundPositionDefault.title: Background Position(s)
semComposition_backgroundPositionDefault.description: Location(s) of off-peak background measurement(s) relative to the peak, in mm or sin-theta, and whether on the high- or low-energy side.

semComposition_beamDamageMinimizationDef.title: Beam Damage Minimization
semComposition_beamDamageMinimizationDef.description: Describes any measures taken to reduce electron beam damage to the sample during analysis. Examples: reduced accelerating voltage, lowered beam current, defocused or rastered beam, cooled stage, short acquisition sequences, or rotating between multiple points.

semComposition_beamRasterDimensionsDefau.title: Beam Raster Dimensions
semComposition_beamRasterDimensionsDefau.description: Dimensions of the small area over which the beam is rastered at a single analysis point, reported as width × height in µm. Applicable when Beam Mode = Rastered; defines the effective spatial footprint of the measurement. Not applicable when mapping.

semComposition_blankCorrectionDefault.title: Blank Correction
semComposition_blankCorrectionDefault.description: Method and reference material(s) used to determine and subtract blank signal contributions (e.g., carbon coat contribution to C signal, or background contamination for trace elements).

semComposition_chamberPressureDefault.title: Chamber Pressure
semComposition_chamberPressureDefault.description: Chamber pressure and gas type during analysis. Required for variable pressure (VP-SEM) and environmental SEM (ESEM) modes. Report value and unit (Pa or Torr) and gas composition. Use 'None' for standard high-vacuum operation.

semComposition_countingStatisticsErrorDe.title: Counting Statistics Error
semComposition_countingStatisticsErrorDe.description: Uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — for each reported quantity per analysis, with the sigma level stated. Derived from the counts on the target species together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. Distinct from the scatter actually observed within a measurement or between repeated measurements, which is recorded separately.

semComposition_detectionLimitDefault.title: Detection Limit
semComposition_detectionLimitDefault.description: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per target species, these being the same set). State the units and whether the values are procedure-typical estimates or session-specific measured values. The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations.

semComposition_driftCorrectionDefault.title: Drift Correction
semComposition_driftCorrectionDefault.description: Describes whether and how stage or beam drift was monitored and corrected during the measurement session. Examples: periodic stage realignment to a fiducial marker, automated beam drift correction in acquisition software, or reanalysis of a reference point at regular intervals.

semComposition_halogenCorrectionOnOxygen.title: Halogen Correction on Oxygen
semComposition_halogenCorrectionOnOxygen.description: Whether oxygen content was adjusted to account for halogen substitution (F and/or Cl replacing OH) in halogen-bearing phases such as apatite, amphibole, and mica, where oxygen is calculated by stoichiometry.

semComposition_normalizationStandardsBas.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction
semComposition_normalizationStandardsBas.description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.

semComposition_preAnalysisImagingAndScre.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
semComposition_preAnalysisImagingAndScre.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

semComposition_timeDependentIntensityCor.title: Time-Dependent Intensity Correction
semComposition_timeDependentIntensityCor.description: Type of time-dependent intensity (TDI) correction applied to compensate for beam-induced volatilisation or migration of sensitive elements (e.g., Na, K, F in glasses, feldspars, carbonates).

semFibsem_preAnalysisImagingAndScreening.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
semFibsem_preAnalysisImagingAndScreening.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

semImaging_chamberPressureDefault.title: Chamber Pressure
semImaging_chamberPressureDefault.description: Chamber pressure and gas type during analysis. Required for variable pressure (VP-SEM) and environmental SEM (ESEM) modes. Report value and unit (Pa or Torr) and gas composition. Use 'None' for standard high-vacuum operation.

semImaging_clWavelengthCalibrationRefere.title: CL Wavelength Calibration Reference
semImaging_clWavelengthCalibrationRefere.description: Reference light source or standard material used to calibrate the wavelength axis of the CL spectrometer. Required for quantitative spectral CL and hyperspectral mapping.

semImaging_ebsdFrameTimeDefault.title: EBSD Frame Time
semImaging_ebsdFrameTimeDefault.description: Acquisition time per EBSD diffraction pattern frame in milliseconds.

semImaging_ebsdPatternQualityThresholdDe.title: EBSD Pattern Quality Threshold
semImaging_ebsdPatternQualityThresholdDe.description: Minimum pattern quality or confidence index threshold applied during EBSD data processing to exclude unreliably indexed points from orientation maps. Include metric name and threshold value.

semImaging_imagePixelSizeDefault.title: Image Pixel Size
semImaging_imagePixelSizeDefault.description: Physical size of each image pixel at the sample surface, in nm or µm. For large-area mosaic imaging, report the pixel size of individual tiles and the number and arrangement of tiles.

semImaging_preAnalysisImagingAndScreenin.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
semImaging_preAnalysisImagingAndScreenin.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.

sem_analyticalAccuracyDefault.title: Analytical Accuracy
sem_analyticalAccuracyDefault.description: Offset between measured and accepted reference values for secondary standards, expressed as percent relative bias. Include reference material, reference value source, and the measured value.

sem_analyticalPrecisionDefault.title: Analytical Precision
sem_analyticalPrecisionDefault.description: Reproducibility of repeated measurements on the same or equivalent reference material, expressed as 1-sigma relative standard deviation (%). Include reference material name, number of analyses (n), and the measured value.

sem_backgroundPositionDefault.title: Background Position(s)
sem_backgroundPositionDefault.description: Location(s) of off-peak background measurement(s) relative to the peak, in mm or sin-theta, and whether on the high- or low-energy side.

sem_beamDamageMinimizationDefault.title: Beam Damage Minimization
sem_beamDamageMinimizationDefault.description: Describes any measures taken to reduce electron beam damage to the sample during analysis. Examples: reduced accelerating voltage, lowered beam current, defocused or rastered beam, cooled stage, short acquisition sequences, or rotating between multiple points.

sem_beamRasterDimensionsDefault.title: Beam Raster Dimensions
sem_beamRasterDimensionsDefault.description: Dimensions of the small area over which the beam is rastered at a single analysis point, reported as width × height in µm. Applicable when Beam Mode = Rastered; defines the effective spatial footprint of the measurement. Not applicable when mapping.

sem_blankCorrectionDefault.title: Blank Correction
sem_blankCorrectionDefault.description: Method and reference material(s) used to determine and subtract blank signal contributions (e.g., carbon coat contribution to C signal, or background contamination for trace elements).

sem_chamberPressureDefault.title: Chamber Pressure

sem_clWavelengthCalibrationReferenceDefa.title: CL Wavelength Calibration Reference
sem_clWavelengthCalibrationReferenceDefa.description: Reference light source or standard material used to calibrate the wavelength axis of the CL spectrometer. Required for quantitative spectral CL and hyperspectral mapping.

sem_countingStatisticsErrorDefault.title: Counting Statistics Error
sem_countingStatisticsErrorDefault.description: Uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — for each reported quantity per analysis, with the sigma level stated. Derived from the counts on the target species together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. sem_detectionLimitDefault.title: Detection Limit
sem_detectionLimitDefault.description: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per target species, these being the same set). State the units and whether the values are procedure-typical estimates or session-specific measured values. The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations.

sem_driftCorrectionDefault.title: Drift Correction
sem_driftCorrectionDefault.description: Describes whether and how stage or beam drift was monitored and corrected during the measurement session. sem_ebsdFrameTimeDefault.title: EBSD Frame Time
sem_ebsdFrameTimeDefault.description: Acquisition time per EBSD diffraction pattern frame in milliseconds.

sem_ebsdPatternQualityThresholdDefault.title: EBSD Pattern Quality Threshold
sem_ebsdPatternQualityThresholdDefault.description: Minimum pattern quality or confidence index threshold applied during EBSD data processing to exclude unreliably indexed points from orientation maps. Include metric name and threshold value.

sem_halogenCorrectionOnOxygenDefault.title: Halogen Correction on Oxygen
sem_halogenCorrectionOnOxygenDefault.description: Whether oxygen content was adjusted to account for halogen substitution (F and/or Cl replacing OH) in halogen-bearing phases such as apatite, amphibole, and mica, where oxygen is calculated by stoichiometry.

sem_imagePixelSizeDefault.title: Image Pixel Size

sem_normalizationStandardsBasedCorrectio.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction

Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.

sem_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDefaul.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening
sem_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDefaul.description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the sampling unit to be analysed, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. sem_timeDependentIntensityCorrectionDefa.title: Time-Dependent Intensity Correction
sem_timeDependentIntensityCorrectionDefa.description: Type of time-dependent intensity (TDI) correction applied to compensate for beam-induced volatilisation or migration of sensitive elements (e.g., Na, K, F in glasses, feldspars, carbonates).

sims_preAnalysisImagingAndScreeningDefau.title: Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening

solutionMcicpms_countingStatisticsErrorD.title: Counting Statistics Error

solutionMcicpms_doubleSpikeMixingRatioDe.title: Double-Spike Mixing Ratio
solutionMcicpms_doubleSpikeMixingRatioDe.description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total target species signal in the spiked mixture, expressed as spike fraction (0–1) or spike:sample ratio. solutionMcicpms_doublyChargedSpeciesMoni.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor

solutionMcicpms_doublyChargedSpeciesProd.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production

solutionMcicpms_errorCorrelationBetweenR.title: Error Correlation Between Reported Quantities

solutionMcicpms_icpTuningDefault.title: ICP Tuning

solutionMcicpms_makeUpGasAndFlowRateDefa.title: Make-up Gas and Flow Rate

solutionMcicpms_memoryEffectMitigationDe.title: Memory Effect Mitigation

At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.

solutionMcicpms_normalizationStandardsBa.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction

solutionMcicpms_reactionGasFlowRateDefau.title: Reaction Gas Flow Rate

solutionMcicpms_sampleAliquotMassOrVolum.title: Sample Aliquot Mass or Volume

solutionMcicpms_spikeOutlierFilteringApp.title: Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach

solutionMcicpms_torchDepthDefault.title: Torch Depth

solutionMcicpms_uncertaintyPropagationMe.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
